components.name: Test-driven development
components.description: A compact test-driven development agreement for feature and bug-fix work.

selection.when: You want test-first feature and bug-fix work and have a practical test environment.
selection.consider: Skip for exploratory work if test order is not a standing project policy.
selection.example: A parser bug gets a failing regression test before the fix.

components.outcome: Features and bug fixes begin with a behavioral test and finish with relevant checks passing.
components.alwaysOnJustification: The agreement changes implementation order throughout feature and bug-fix work.

components.name: Minimal implementation
components.description: Keep implementations to the smallest safe change that meets current requirements.

selection.when: Changes keep acquiring unused abstractions, wrappers, or dependencies.
selection.consider: State planned extension points as requirements; a small diff alone is not proof of correctness.
selection.example: Reuse the existing HTTP client instead of adding a provider framework.

components.outcome: Changes meet current requirements without speculative code, dependencies, or abstraction.
components.alwaysOnJustification: The rule applies whenever an agent chooses an implementation approach.

components.name: Completion evidence
components.description: Require concrete checks and transparent reporting before claiming completion.

selection.when: Handoffs leave you unsure which checks actually ran.
selection.consider: Adds reporting to every handoff.
selection.example: A UI handoff names the tests and browser checks run, plus anything skipped.

components.outcome: Completion claims identify the checks run, failures encountered, and verification skipped, and lead with anything waiting on the user.
components.alwaysOnJustification: The rule applies to the completion of every repository task.

components.name: Transparent shortcuts
components.description: Make deliberately deferred necessary work visible without inventing speculative debt.

selection.when: Necessary work is deliberately postponed during delivery.
selection.consider: Do not turn speculative future features into debt or duplicate an existing tracking process.
selection.example: Record the reason and risk when a required retry path is deferred.

components.outcome: Material deferred work is visible with a concrete reason and risk.
components.alwaysOnJustification: The rule must be available when task scope and implementation tradeoffs are decided.

components.name: Secure defaults
components.description: Apply concise preventive safeguards at new external boundaries.

selection.when: You add APIs, file imports, or sensitive operations across trust boundaries.
selection.consider: Does not replace a threat model or define your actual roles, limits, and authentication choices.
selection.example: An upload endpoint checks caller permissions, file type, and size limits.

components.outcome: New trust boundaries validate and constrain input, avoid injection, keep secrets out of code and logs, protect mutations, and use least privilege.
components.alwaysOnJustification: In repositories with external boundaries, the safeguards affect design before code is written.

components.name: No unfinished UI
components.description: Do not expose incomplete product paths without an explicit product reason.

selection.when: Released interfaces should expose only usable product paths.
selection.consider: Exploratory prototypes and explicitly required disabled states may need a different policy.
selection.example: Omit an export button until export works, unless the product requires a disabled state.

components.outcome: Users see coherent product paths rather than nonfunctional controls or placeholders.
components.alwaysOnJustification: When adopted as product policy, the rule applies across all frontend implementation work.

components.name: Focused changes
components.description: Keep edits within the requested outcome, preserve unrelated work, and clean up code made unused by the change.

selection.when: You want a standing policy against incidental cleanup, formatting, and unrelated edits during implementation.
selection.consider: Skip if equivalent project guidance already applies. Necessary supporting refactors and explicitly requested cleanup remain allowed.
selection.example: A parser fix removes its newly unused import while leaving unrelated comments, formatting, and user edits intact.

components.outcome: Changes include necessary supporting work without incidental cleanup or damage to unrelated user work.
components.alwaysOnJustification: The policy governs the scope of edits throughout implementation, before any review workflow is invoked.

components.name: Autonomy
components.description: Keep working through steps that need no input; stop only when blocked or before destructive actions.

selection.when: You hand agents whole tasks with a clear finish line and want them to run without check-ins.
selection.consider: Skip for pair programming, where you want a summary before and after each action.
selection.example: A migration runs to passing tests, then stops to ask before dropping the old table.

components.outcome: Agents finish independent steps without pausing and ask only when blocked or before destructive or outward-facing actions.
components.alwaysOnJustification: The rule decides whether to continue or ask at every step of every task.

components.name: Durable task list
components.description: Track long multi-step work in a root TASKS.md so progress survives context resets.

selection.when: Agents run long multi-step tasks that can outlast their context window.
selection.consider: Adds a TASKS.md file to the repository root during work; skip if your agent's built-in task tracking is enough.
selection.example: A twelve-endpoint migration lists each endpoint in TASKS.md and checks them off, so a new session resumes at the next one.

components.outcome: Long tasks keep a current checklist in TASKS.md that a fresh session can resume from.
components.alwaysOnJustification: The agent must know the convention before a long task starts, not after its context is lost.

components.name: Documentation audit
components.description: Audit documentation for accuracy, staleness, duplication, broken references, and unnecessary context cost.

selection.when: Setup instructions, links, or repository docs may have drifted from the code.
selection.consider: Reports evidence and recommended fixes; editing needs a separate request.
selection.example: Ask: Use audit-docs to check our README and contributor documentation.

components.name: Terraform skill
components.description: Version-aware Terraform and OpenTofu guidance with complete upstream references.

selection.when: You maintain Terraform or OpenTofu configuration and need version-aware guidance.
selection.consider: Downloads upstream content and references when selected. Guidance must match installed tool versions.
selection.example: Ask: Use terraform-skill to review this module against our pinned Terraform version.

components.name: FastAPI
components.description: Official, version-aware FastAPI guidance with complete upstream references.

selection.when: You build or maintain a FastAPI application.
selection.consider: Downloads upstream content and references when selected. Check advice against the project version.
selection.example: Ask: Use fastapi to implement a validated endpoint using our installed version.

components.name: Codebase design
components.description: Shared vocabulary and principles for designing deep modules, placing seams, and keeping interfaces testable.

selection.when: You design or restructure module interfaces, look for modules to deepen, or decide where a seam belongs.
selection.consider: Downloads upstream content and references when selected. Uses a fixed vocabulary (module, interface, seam, adapter); its Design It Twice process runs parallel sub-agents when asked to compare interfaces.
selection.example: Ask: Use codebase-design to find shallow modules worth deepening in src/.

components.name: TDD workflow
components.description: Red-green test-driven workflow with guidance on test seams, mocking, and test anti-patterns.

selection.when: You build features or fix bugs test-first and want guidance on where tests go and which tests are worth keeping.
selection.consider: Downloads upstream content and references when selected. Adds on-demand detail to block/tdd. Asks you to agree the seams under test when the task does not establish them, and uses codebase-design for interface vocabulary when it is installed.
selection.example: Ask: Use tdd to add the discount rule test-first.

components.name: Commit work
components.description: Review, validate, and create one focused Git commit while preserving unrelated work.

selection.when: A focused change is ready to validate and commit.
selection.consider: Creates a Git commit when invoked; preserves unrelated work and does not push automatically.
selection.example: Invoke commit-work to review, validate, and commit the current focused change.

components.name: Frontend design
components.description: Official Claude plugin for production-grade frontend design.

selection.when: You use Claude and want its frontend design plugin available.
selection.consider: Requires Claude. Installation enables the plugin; it does not build or verify your interface.
selection.example: Use the design plugin in Claude while building a new product page.

components.name: TypeScript LSP
components.description: Official Claude TypeScript language-server integration.

selection.when: You use Claude on JavaScript or TypeScript projects with a language server.
selection.consider: Requires typescript-language-server on PATH; this installer does not install that executable.
selection.example: Enable language-server support for a TypeScript project in Claude.

suggest.reason: TypeScript and its language server detected

components.name: Pyright LSP
components.description: Official Claude Python type-checking integration.

selection.when: You use Claude on Python projects and already have Pyright installed.
selection.consider: Requires pyright-langserver on PATH; this installer does not install that executable.
selection.example: Enable Python type-checking integration for your Claude workflow.

components.name: GitHub
components.description: Official Claude integration for GitHub issues, pull requests, and actions; authentication is configured separately.

selection.when: You use Claude to work with GitHub issues, pull requests, and actions.
selection.consider: GitHub authentication is configured separately; enabling settings does not authenticate you.
selection.example: Connect GitHub in Claude, then ask it to inspect a pull request.

components.name: Codex for Claude
components.description: Claude plugin that exposes an existing Codex CLI for delegation and code review.

selection.when: You use Claude and already have the Codex CLI for review or delegated work.
selection.consider: Requires codex on PATH and separate runtime setup; it does not install the Codex CLI.
selection.example: Use the plugin from Claude to request a second review through your Codex CLI.
